title: Saemisch (5.f3) & Four Pawns (5.f4)
intro: Meet the Saemisch (5.f3) with ...O-O and ...e5 or ...c5. Counter the Four Pawns Attack (5.f4) with ...O-O, ...c5 and ...e6.
variation: d2d4 g8f6 c2c4 g7g6 b1c3 f8g7 e2e4 d7d6 f2f3, d2d4 g8f6 c2c4 g7g6 b1c3 f8g7 e2e4 d7d6 f2f4

lessons.title: Meeting the Saemisch (5.f3)
lessons.summary: Castle, strike with 6...e5, and play ...Nh5 against 7.d5.

steps.text: In the Saemisch Variation (5.f3), White guards e4 solidly and plans Be3, Qd2 and O-O-O.
Get your king safe before opening the centre.
steps.ifRight: Now Black is ready to strike.

steps.text: Strike in the centre immediately while White's kingside is undeveloped.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...e5 to challenge d4 at once.
steps.ifRight: White must decide whether to push d5 or develop Nge2.

steps.text: Clear the way for ...f5 and eye the f4 square.
steps.hint: Jump to h5 with your f6 knight.
steps.ifRight: Next ...f5 attacks White's centre and kingside.

steps.text: If White develops 7.Nge2 instead of 7.d5, open the centre before White castles.
steps.hint: Capture on d4 so you can break with ...c6 and ...d5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7...exd4 (followed by ...c6 and ...d5) to open lines in the middle.
steps.ifRight: After 8.Nxd4 c6 9.Qd2 d5, Black equalizes actively in the centre.

lessons.title: Meeting 6.Bg5
lessons.summary: Counter 6.Bg5 with 6...c5 and undermine d5 with ...e6.

steps.text: Against 5...O-O, White sometimes pins the knight with 6.Bg5.
Hit White's centre from the c-file while the c1 bishop left b2 behind.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...c5 to attack d4 and open the long diagonal.
steps.ifRight: If White takes on c5, ...Qa5 or ...dxc5 regains the pawn easily.

steps.text: Attack the d5 pawn right away.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7...e6 to trade on d5 and open lines against White's uncastled king.
steps.ifRight: Black opens the e-file and activates the g7 bishop.

steps.ifWrong: Play 8...exd5: after 9.cxd5, Black plays ...Re8 and ...a6 with active counterplay.
steps.ifRight: Black gets great play down the e-file and on the queenside with ...a6 and ...b5.

lessons.title: The Four Pawns Attack (5.f4)
lessons.summary: Castle, strike with 6...c5, and break open the centre with 7...e6.

steps.text: In the Four Pawns Attack, White builds a huge pawn wall, leaving the king in the centre and dark squares loose.

steps.ifRight: Now Black strikes at White's overextended centre.

steps.text: Attack the d4 pawn before White finishes development.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6...c5: if White captures 7.dxc5, 7...Qa5 threatens ...Nxe4 and ...Qxc5.
steps.ifRight: Black undermines White's giant centre right away.

steps.text: Challenge d5 immediately while White's king is still on e1.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7...e6: after ...exd5 cxd5, ...Re8 puts immediate pressure on e4.
steps.ifRight: After 8.Be2 exd5 9.cxd5 Re8, e4 is under heavy pressure.
